actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is an example of creating a custom MuJoCo model and training a reinforcement-learning agent with the Gymnasium shell and StableBaselines

The README describes a ball-balancing environment with a 10-value observation (position and speed for rotating the platform along two axes and moving the ball along three axes), a reward of 1 per step and episodes of 500 steps by default
BallBalanceEnv subclasses gymnasium's MujocoEnv and utils.EzPickle
BallBalanceEnv loads the MJCF model at os.path.abspath('assets/ball_balance.xml') and constructs MujocoEnv with frame_skip 5
The observation space is an unbounded 10-value Box of float64
The default episode length is 500 steps
The environment returns a constant reward of 1.0 and terminates when the observation is not finite or its third value obs[2] is below 0
The environment truncates once step_number exceeds episode_len
The environment's observation concatenates the ball's first three qpos values, its first three qvel values, and the qpos and qvel of rotate_x and rotate_y
The model's box body has two hinge joints rotate_x and rotate_y on the x and y axes, each with range -.25 to .25 and damping 20
The model's ball body has a freejoint named ball and a sphere geom of radius .05
The model has two general actuators, act_x on rotate_x and act_y on rotate_y, each with ctrlrange -1 to 1 and gainprm '1000 0 0'
model_viewer.py loads the XML with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, creates mujoco.MjData, steps with mujoco.mj_step and reads model.opt.timestep

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one data state; cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults and the bridge takes no seed input, so a run repeats exactly on the same engine.  The fake stand-in is deterministic too, but its trajectories are not MuJoCo's.

gaps: the deployed model is MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics with contacts (F1), but the fake backend is a pure-Python stand-in for the mujoco library: it parses the MJCF for the joint count, actuator count, control ranges and start positions and integrates a placeholder first-order hinge motion plus a placeholder free fall, not MuJoCo's equations, contacts, friction, actuator forces, sensors or noise

MuJoCo was not installed where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; the fake's 2 ms timestep is a placeholder for MuJoCo's library default because the model sets no <option timestep>

the bridge serves the raw MuJoCo world: observation is the simulator's time/qpos/qvel and the state adds ctrl/tick/timestep/seed; BallBalanceEnv's 10-value observation selection, constant reward 1.0, obs[2] < 0 termination and 500-step truncation (ball_balance_env.py:20-44, :62-68) are not applied by this driver
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no rendering, camera or visualisation is offered; the MJCF's camera, texture and light are part of the model tree but are not rendered by the bridge
snapshot and restore use the bridge's fallback copy of time/qpos/qvel/ctrl (the stand-in has no mj_getState/mj_setState), so a restore is not the full integration state of the real engine

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
